title: listWithSelectors: transport errors vs embedded search errors
answers: Why did a search outage/cancellation during LIST not get retried by the client?
A failed search query returned an empty successful list instead of an error
How should gRPC search client responses be converted into ListResponse?
body:
Symptom: when the remote search backend was unavailable or a query failed, listWithSelectors previously either (a) wrapped a transport error (e.g. codes.Unavailable, cancellation) into an otherwise-successful ListResponse, defeating the unified client's retry interceptor, or (b) read rows from a response whose embedded ResourceSearchResponse.Error was set, returning an empty list as if it succeeded.
Root cause: pkg/storage/unified/resource/list_with_selectors.go:listWithSelectors called ErrorFromResponse on the gRPC call's own err, and never checked searchResp.GetError() at all.
Fix pattern: return the raw transport err immediately (err != nil => return nil, err) before touching the response body; only after a successful call, check searchResp.GetError() and convert it via AsErrorResult into resp.Error (not into a Go error) so the response shape expected by callers is preserved.
Constraints: applies to any server-side RPC fan-out where a nested response carries its own Error field distinct from the transport error; do not merge the two error sources into one check.
